appraisal_events.evidence: « Le dreyfusisme avait rendu Swann d’une naïveté extraordinaire […] se montrait pourtant d’un aveuglement comique », his political and literary judgments all retested by « un critérium nouveau, le dreyfusisme », and his denial « Non, je ne vous ai jamais dit autrement. Vous confondez. »; qualified by « ce nouveau déclassement eût été mieux appelé reclassement et n’était qu’honorable pour lui ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's dominant act is a comic exposure of Swann: his admirations and disdains are shown to be mechanically re-sorted by a single new criterion, and he cannot even remember his own reversed opinions. The same commentary grants him an honorable ancestral reclassement and a lucidity ahead of society, so the movement is double-edged but its governing body and tone are diminishing.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Cela me fait grand plaisir. Cela ne m’étonne pas, il est très intelligent. C’est beaucoup, cela », set against « sa mère est très contre »; and « il a du reste passé comme une lettre à la poste » at the Jockey — « Malgré l’Affaire ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann explicitly credits Saint-Loup with intelligence, marking him off favorably from his antidreyfusard mother, and Saint-Loup's effortless election to the Jockey confirms his standing despite the Affair. The narrator immediately ironizes such verdicts as products of Swann's dreyfusard criterion, which qualifies the source without cancelling Saint-Loup's local gain.

status_effects.explanation: Swann comes off locally worse: the narrator calls his new outlook an extraordinary naïveté and a comic blindness, even while conceding that the shift itself is honorable.
His authority as a judge collapses in the passage: his political and literary pronouncements are shown to be dictated by one criterion, and he flatly denies ever having said the opposite.
Saint-Loup is praised as very intelligent and singled out approvingly against his mother's opposite position.
He is admitted to the Jockey effortlessly, and the surprise at his passing despite the Affair underscores that his social inclusion is unharmed by his dreyfusism.

ambiguities: The narrator's verdict on Swann is explicitly double: the same sentence that calls his dreyfusism a déclassement recasts it as an honorable reclassement toward his ancestral line and credits him with seeing a truth hidden from society people, before pivoting to « un aveuglement comique ». Reading the honorable clause as the main point would invert Swann's delta to positive; the reading taken here treats the comic exposure as the passage's dominant body.

It is undecidable whether Swann's « il est très intelligent » about Saint-Loup is a genuine appraisal or purely an instance of the mechanical dreyfusard criterion the narrator mocks two sentences later (as with Mme Bontemps found « bête »). That choice governs whether E2 counts as real admiration or as ironized reflex, and hence the size of Saint-Loup's gain.
